ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary federal AML/CFT legislation is the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA), and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184, as amended. Reporting-entity obligations are administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). The Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, including terrorist-property provisions, the United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2, and the Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17, support sanctions controls. Alberta limited partnerships are principally governed by the Alberta Partnership Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. P-3. Canada has no general publicly searchable federal UBO register applicable to Alberta limited partnerships. Federal corporations are subject to beneficial-ownership record requirements under the Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, sections 21.1-21.303, but those provisions do not create a general public UBO register for an Alberta limited partnership. Corporate registries, financial institutions, regulated professionals, and FINTRAC reporting entities may require ownership and control information under applicable law and risk-based procedures.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screen all UBOs, partners, directors, officers, authorized signatories, major counterparties, payment providers, and relevant beneficial owners before onboarding and periodically thereafter. Screening must cover Canadian sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and related regulations; United Nations Security Council lists; applicable OFAC sanctions where there is a United States nexus, United States payment processing, United States persons, or United States-origin technology; and PEP, head-of-international-organization, family-member, and close-associate indicators under PCMLTFA requirements. Resolve false positives using documentary evidence, retain audit trails, apply enhanced due diligence to high-risk persons and jurisdictions, and report suspicious transactions or terrorist-property matches as legally required. A Canadian private LP is not automatically a FINTRAC reporting entity solely because it operates a video-chat application; obligations arise if it conducts activities covered by the PCMLTFA, including prescribed money services, remittance, virtual-currency, or other regulated financial activities.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry, accessed through an authorized Alberta registry agent and the Alberta.ca Corporate Registry services
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered LP name must comply with the Alberta Partnership Act and registry requirements, be distinguishable from existing registered names, and not be misleading or confusing. English-language names are accepted. French or other-language elements may be used if accurately represented and not misleading. A translated or alternate business name may require separate registration. Non-Latin characters and transliterations should be confirmed with the registry agent before filing. A numbered limited partnership name may be used where an acceptable descriptive name is unavailable or not desired. The name should not imply incorporation, government affiliation, professional authorization, banking, insurance, or a regulated activity that the partnership does not hold.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Institute where it implies an educational institution
Professional titles or regulated-profession terms implying authorization
Words suggesting a licensed financial, charitable, health, educational, or governmental status
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain a NUANS or equivalent Alberta name search and submit the proposed LP name through an authorized registry agent. If the registry rejects the name, request the written rejection reason and identify the governing statutory or administrative ground. File a corrected name, consent, or supporting authorization where the issue is a sensitive term, existing-name conflict, or regulated-word restriction. Alberta registry decisions are generally administrative and may not have a specific statutory appeal route for every name-screening decision. Escalate first through the registry agent and Alberta Corporate Registry review channel; if the decision is legally unreasonable, procedurally unfair, or based on an error of law, obtain Alberta counsel advice regarding judicial review in the Alberta Court of King's Bench within the applicable limitation period. Do not market or execute contracts under the rejected name while review is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: An Alberta LP must maintain the registered office and filing information required by the Alberta Partnership Act and the Alberta Corporate Registry. A commercial virtual office may generally be used for registry correspondence if it is a genuine service address, the provider is authorized to receive service and official notices, and the arrangement satisfies registry-agent, banking, tax, privacy, and AML requirements. A mailbox-only address, accommodation address, or address incapable of receiving legal service is unsuitable. For a cross-border video-chat application, the virtual office does not by itself establish operational substance, management, employees, technology control, data-governance capability, or tax residence. Payment providers, banks, Apple, and Paymentwall may require evidence of actual operations, management location, contracts, beneficial ownership, and customer-support capability.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for ordinary Alberta LP registration because there is no routine statutory pre-registration site inspection; no official probability is published. Internal compliance estimate for an unannounced physical verification or address challenge is approximately 5-15% in a low-risk profile and higher where the structure involves foreign UBOs, high-risk jurisdictions, payment processing, complaints, suspected misrepresentation, sanctions alerts, or an address shared by numerous entities. Banks, payment processors, tax authorities, FINTRAC, and law-enforcement bodies may conduct separate verification or request documentary and in-person evidence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, Part 2 (Limited Partnerships), as amended
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Partnership Act. A limited partner must contribute cash, property, or services to acquire limited partner status; no escrow account is mandated. Advisors may use an escrow arrangement for future capital calls.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the undersigned general partner and initial limited partner(s) do hereby adopt and pass the following resolutions as the First Board Resolution of CA__CA_AB__CA_LP__ISIC_6311_02_RANDOM_VIDEO_MATCH_APP (the 'Partnership'): (1) SUBSCRIPTION: the initial capital contributions set forth in the partnership subscription schedule are approved and accepted; (2) REGISTERED OFFICE: the registered office shall be located at the address of the Partnership's registered agent in Alberta, and the registered agent is appointed; (3) OFFICERS: [insert name] is appointed authorized signing officer and record-keeping officer for filings with the Alberta Corporate Registry; (4) AUTHORIZATION: the officers are directed to file the Declaration of Limited Partnership and to take all actions necessary to implement this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – Name Approval Service (via authorized NUANS providers)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for the proposed limited partnership name; if the name is distinguishable and compliant with provincial naming rules, obtain a name reservation and record the reservation number for use in the Declaration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for similarity or misdescriptiveness, select an alternate name from the NUANS list and re-file; an applicant may request Director's review under the Partnership Act within 30 days of the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed legal practitioner or notary public; all initial partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement and the Declaration of Limited Partnership. Ensure the Declaration states the partnership name, registered office in Alberta, registered agent address, full names and addresses of all general and limited partners, and the amount of capital contributed. Have all partners execute the documents before a witness or notary.
required_dossiers: Passport or government-issued identification of each partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If execution is defective or a partner fails to sign, redraft the relevant page and re-execute before a notary; a defective filing can be withdrawn and re-submitted with a new declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) – online portal or physical counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Declaration of Limited Partnership through the Alberta corporate registry electronic portal or at a Service Alberta counter. Pay the prescribed filing fee and retain the stamped or electronic filing acknowledgement as proof of registration.
required_dossiers: Prescribed filing fee (C$60 or current schedule)
Agent authorization if filing through a law firm or corporate agent
Consent to act of the registered agent and office owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or correction notice, file a corrected declaration or a formal explanation within 30 calendar days; if denied, apply for ministerial review or seek judicial review in the Court of King's Bench.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the registered office is located within Alberta and that the registered agent has consented to act. The registered agent and office address must be recorded in the Declaration or, if changed after initial filing, in a Notice of Change.
required_dossiers: Written Consent to Act as Registered Agent
Proof of registered office address (e.g., lease or utility bill)
Declaration of Limited Partnership showing registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent resigns or the office becomes invalid, file a Notice of Change of Registered Office/Agent within 30 days; in case of dispute, court order from the Court of King's Bench may be sought.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Activation and Business Number Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; Canada Revenue Agency (federal complement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Certificate of Registration is issued, obtain the Alberta corporate access number. Where needed, register the limited partnership with the Canada Revenue Agency for a Business Number, GST/HST, payroll, and any required import/export accounts.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Partner identification and partnership agreement excerpts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA rejects an account application due to name mismatch or missing information, correct the legal entity particulars and re-apply via the CRA My Business Account portal or submit a written objection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No provincial industrial licensing board applies to ISIC 6311 (data processing, hosting and online video matching); if a physical office or studio is opened, municipal licensing authorities in Calgary, Edmonton, or the relevant Alberta municipality will apply.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable for pure online video matching; a general municipal business licence may be required for any physical commercial premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the platform is an online service without industrial discharge; if a dedicated data centre or server storage site is established, a screening assessment may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For any supporting physical infrastructure, compliance with the Alberta Air Quality Objectives, Wastewater Regulation (Alberta Environment and Protected Areas), and the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 VOC and hazardous waste standards would be required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For office or server-room premises: fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code (Safety Codes Council), structural load inspection for equipment installations, and occupational health and safety clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (Alberta).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal income tax, GST/HST and Business Number; Alberta Provincial Tax Authority has no separate income tax jurisdiction. Official portals: canada.ca/cra and mybusinessaccount.cra.gc.ca
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Domestic Canadian Limited Partnerships obtain Business Number (BN) via CRA online portal or Form RC1. Non-resident partners may require separate registration; GST/HST registration triggered by exceeding CAD 30,000 annual taxable supplies in Canada through CRA My Account or designated agent
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No federal check-the-box election available; tax classification determined by Alberta Partnership Act and federal rules. Hybrid mismatch and GAAR rules apply for cross-border structuring

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 annual taxable supplies in Canada
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time digital reporting and clearance via CRA systems under GST/HST New Registration and Filing Rules; API integration required for electronic invoicing and digital stamping of compliant tax invoices

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% GST rate on exports of goods and services to non-residents outside Canada, including offshore digital services, provided supply is exported and not consumed in Canada; requires proof of export for goods and non-residential use for services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits may result in reassessment; penalties under Excise Tax Act include fines up to 50% of evaded tax, interest charges, and potential criminal prosecution for fraudulent claims; retrospective clawback of zero-rated amounts if export not substantiated

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign-exchange policy is administered jointly with the Minister of Finance, while AML/EFT supervision of financial institutions is shared by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully and freely convertible under Canada's IMF Article VIII obligations; no exchange-control approvals apply to capital or current-account transactions. Profit remittance by an Alberta Limited Partnership to non-resident partners is subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax of 25% on the partner's Canadian-source business income share, unless reduced or eliminated under an applicable income tax treaty (e.g., Canada-US Convention). Non-resident partners may file a Canadian income tax return to claim treaty relief; there are no other legal restrictions on transferring funds abroad after Canadian tax obligations are settled.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion requirements. Exporters and service providers may retain and freely dispose of foreign-currency earnings; however, for income tax purposes, foreign-currency receipts must be translated into Canadian dollars using the Bank of Canada daily exchange rate or another acceptable rate for reporting.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Low. An offshore e-money institution (EMI) holding a non-Canadian authorization (for example, a UK FCA EMI licence) is not a recognized deposit-taking institution in Canada and cannot independently operate payment accounts or hold client funds within the country. To process the target payment rails (Apple IAP and Paymentwall), the Canadian LP must route through either a regulated Canadian bank or a FINTRAC-registered money services business (MSB) that is also authorized under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) administered by the Bank of Canada. The offshore EMI may serve only as a white-label technology or card-processing supplier, but it must not touch the LP's funds or Canadian user funds unless it itself is FINTRAC-registered and RPAA-licensed.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote video onboarding is generally accepted by the major Canadian banks for directors and authorized signatories; however, due to the Medium-Risk Enhanced AML tier of the video-matching application, the bank's financial crime compliance unit will likely mandate a video-call interview with the General Partner's authorized representatives and a beneficial-ownership attestation. Certified original documents (passport, Alberta Partnership Registration, Partnership Agreement, annual returns) must be supplied. For signatories located outside Canada, notarized identity certificates issued by a notary public or a Canadian legal counsel letter are typically required. In-person board attendance is not a universal statutory mandate, but banks retain discretion to require an in-branch meeting for enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual credit / in-app token microtransactions routed through Apple IAP and Paymentwall creating a money-laundering layering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML/ATF policy manual; transaction-monitoring thresholds and velocity limits for user accounts; mandatory user KYC/ID verification; segregation of user float from corporate operating funds; SOC 2 Type II report; FINTRAC MSB/e-submitter registration evidence; publicly available privacy policy and terms of service.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border random video matching exposing the platform to sanctions-evasion or high-risk jurisdiction traffic.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IP geoblocking of comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions (Canada, United Nations, and OFAC lists); real-time denial-list screening; negative-media and PEP monitoring procedures; Global Affairs Canada sanctions and export-control assessment; audit trails of blocked sessions with timestamps and user identifiers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque limited-partner beneficial-ownership structure due to non-resident partners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed and notarized partnership agreement; register of partners showing capital-contribution history; beneficial-ownership declarations aligned with FINTRAC guidance; source-of-funds evidence (bank statements and corporate filings); Canadian Business Number and tax identification for each partner; written confirmation that no politically exposed foreign person controls the Limited Partnership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High chargeback and refund velocity inherent in social-technology in-app purchases.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI-DSS Level 1 attestation; merchant-acquirer risk-management policies; chargeback monitoring and ratio-reporting dashboard; refund policy documentation; customer-support dispute-resolution workflow; recurring-billing confirmation logs.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 (or Fedwire/CHIPS for USD) to the LP's dedicated Capital Escrow Account at a Canadian Tier 1 bank, with Field 70 (Remittance Information) clearly indicating 'LP Capital Contribution – [Legal Partnership Name]'. For CAD wires, use the bank's institution/transit/account numbers; for USD, provide the bank's ABA and corresponding SWIFT BIC. Individual transfers of C$10,000 or more trigger FINTRAC EFT reporting, and the bank will require a source-of-funds declaration. The LP must maintain a capital-account ledger, issue contribution receipts to each limited partner, and reconcile all contributions in the partnership's fiscal-period financial statements. The Investment Canada Act review threshold applies only to the acquisition of control of a Canadian business by non-Canadians and is generally not engaged by an inbound capital injection into a newly formed Alberta Limited Partnership; counsel should still confirm the non-Canadian status of contributing partners.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements, content-provider revenue share, or partnership distributions are executed via SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers, CAD domestic large-value transfers via the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) EFT, and USD cross-border payments via SWIFT/CHIPS. Where a disbursance supports a commercial trade (e.g., content licensing or media acquisition), a Commercial Letter of Credit governed by UCP600/eUCP 2.0 may be issued through the bank's trade-services desk. All outgoing instructions must include the beneficiary's full name, account number/IBAN, and SWIFT BIC. OSFI Guideline B-7 requires complete originator information (name, address, account number) for straight-through processing, and cash disbursements are strictly prohibited.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) — permitted only for illiquid or controlled currencies and subject to the bank's prudential credit limits and OSFI risk-management expectations

stage_5.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 – USD 440 per annum (equivalent CAD 250 – CAD 600) for a typical registered agent / registered office arrangement in Alberta
stage_5.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 18,000 for a full IFRS/ASPE audit of a mid-sized LP; USD 2,500 – USD 6,500 for a review engagement; audit not statutorily required in Alberta

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at LP entity level (fiscally transparent); underlying combined federal-provincial corporate rate for a Canadian corporate partner: 15% (federal) + 8% (Alberta) = 23%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No entity-level tax holidays. Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) partners may claim the federal small business deduction (9% federal, 2% Alberta) on qualifying active business income allocated from the LP; flow-through SR&ED investment tax credits may be available per partner. No preferential statutory deduction exists at the LP level.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013 Slips (“Canada Revenue Agency – T5013 Summary and T5013 Schedule”); filed electronically via CRA’s Internet File Transfer (XML) or the CRA My Business Account portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before 5 months after the end of the partnership’s fiscal period (e.g., a December 31 year-end is due May 31 of the following calendar year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business income and deductible operating expenses from the video-match platform (app store fees, payment processing, server costs, subscriber acquisition).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate to each partner according to the partnership agreement. Retain support schedules that separately identify amounts attributable to non-resident partners for their Canadian tax filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 135 – Net Income (Loss) for Income Tax Purposes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership-level net income after applying capital cost allowance, reserves, and any flow-through adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must use this amount to compute Part I taxable income earned in Canada; corporate partners may be subject to Part XIV and treaty provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 155 / Box 156 – Charitable Donations / Political Contributions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Record qualifying donations made by the partnership; these amounts are allocated to partners for their own deduction claims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may claim the deduction only to the extent of their Canadian-source income; provide treaty‑relevant details if requested.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the T5013 Summary/Slips incurs a penalty of CAD 25 per partner per day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500; an additional penalty of CAD 100 per day (maximum CAD 2,500) may apply for failure to file the T5013 Summary electronically. Concurrent interest on any federal tax and gross negligence penalties of 50% of the evasion amount apply. Directors of a corporate general partner can become personally liable for unpaid withholding and penalties if they knowingly participate in the failure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Not applicable to an LP (fiscally transparent entity; distributions are not dividends). Reference: for a Canadian corporation, the statutory Part XIII withholding rate on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders is 25%, with treaty reductions (e.g., 5% for a US corporate shareholder beneficially owning at least 10% of the voting stock, 15% for other US persons; many treaties provide 10%–15%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident partner seeking reduced withholding must submit to the CRA Form NR301 (Application for a Reduction in the Amount of Non-Resident Tax) and obtail a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the partner’s home jurisdiction tax authority. The application must be filed before the relevant payment/realisation date; upon approval the CRA issues a determination of the reduced treaty rate. A partnership must also provide the non-resident’s identifying information on the T5013 summary and supporting schedules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rates: interest – 25% (but interest paid to an arm's length non-resident is generally exempt under the Interest Act and Canada’s domestic exemption); royalty payments – 25% (with treaty reduction typically to 10% for industrial royalties; 0% for certain copyright royalties under select treaties).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is required for designated transactions with non-arm's length non-residents when the aggregate value of such transactions exceeds CAD 1,000,000 in the taxation year. A Master File and Country-by-Country (CbC) Report are mandatory only if the multinational group’s consolidated revenue is at least CAD 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No stand‑alone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) exist in Canada; however, the CRA applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR, s.245 of the Income Tax Act) and the statutory “substance over form” doctrine to disregard transactions that lack genuine commercial substance. Partners and the LP must maintain a real business presence (employees, premises, decision-making) to avoid GAAR reassessments and to secure treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting platform revenue, inflating expenses, or misallocating profits to a non-resident partner to avoid Canadian tax; knowingly signing a false T5013 return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under s.239(1) Income Tax Act: fine between 50% and 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years. Civil penalty for gross negligence: 50% of the understated tax; plus daily late-filing interest and cumulative penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate directors of the general partner and any partner exercising management control may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax, penalties, and interest; courts can pierce the veil to seek restitution. Criminal conviction may trigger travel bans and seizure of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a shell LP with no employees, no Canadian office, or no real operational activity, solely to book Canadian video‑match revenue as foreign income, or to treaty-shop benefits without genuine substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA reassessment under s.245 GAAR denies the tax benefit and imposes interest plus a 50% penalty (exciseable at up to CAD 100,000 per Davidson‑type transaction). In an abusive transfer pricing adjustment, an additional 10% penalty on the net adjustment may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner are exposed to civil liability for reassessed amounts, penalties, and interest if they authorized or allowed the sham structure. Personal travel bans and director prohibition orders may be issued in serious tax-avoidance or evasion cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register with FINTRAC as a Money Service Business (MSB) when the platform facilitates digital payments (e.g., in-app purchases through Apple IAP and Paymentwall) or peer‑to‑peer transfers; failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs), Terrorist Property Reports, or large cash transaction reports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA): administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation for entities and CAD 500,000 for individuals; criminal penalties up to five years’ imprisonment where there is intentional non‑compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and partners who participated in or authorised the non-compliant AML program may be personally liable for FINTRAC sanctions; they may also be subject to travel bans and director disqualification orders where enforcement authorities prosecute.
